Having left your house 2 hours before your flight you now stand waiting in line at the airport to be groped. You pay for the TSA is taxes and think, at least I'm safer now, as they put on the rubber gloves to pat you down. After you collect your meager belongings from the tub you check your watch, awesome 20 minutes before the plane arrives. Just in time to look up and see your son being patted down by a heavy set balding man, he is wearing thick bridged glasses and has a pencil thin moustache. "Great", you think, "my son is being molested". But thanks to the TSA he is going to fly in safety!

"I'm sorry son", you mutter as he stares at the floor following you like a carp seeking its dinner. Clutching your under sized carry on bag, which is the only option you have because paying extra fees for luggage is too much, you make you way to boarding. Finding a seat next to a walrusesque couple you plant yourself to wait out the remaining 10 minutes. Soon over the loud speaker you hear, "flight 122 to Boston will be delayed due to weather concerns". You look at your watch through the streaming sunlight pouring into the large windows over looking the runway... "Ha weather, OK!"

You and your son sit in silence next to your stewing plane mates. "How could they be sweating its 65° in here" you ponder. After what seems an eternity the speaker crackles again, "Now boarding first class". You watch with seething jealousy as 8 people saunter to the front desk to be checked once again. "Now boarding special needs passengers" they announce. Two people slowly move up. Then they start pulling the rows in. Little by little the waiting area empties into the tuna can.

Your going to be late, but that was expected. You will have to also do some shopping when you land. But you are safe. Thanks TSA.
The frustrations are real ... and well, well stated. To the airlines, to the TSA, we are all just cattle.
